newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar touches 1.80 dm, intervention feared.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar touches 1.80 dm, intervention feared.

text.p: The dollar rose briefly above 1.80 marks for the first time in nearly six years and also powered above 115 yen on Tuesday, and foreign exchange dealers trod warily for fear of central bank intervention.

Sterling initially shed around two pfennigs on remarks by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel that dollar and pound strength against the mark was an overreaction and that Germany wanted a strong mark.
"Waigel's comments had only a brief impact but the market is still very nervous about testing 1.80 marks, intervention here is a real prospect," said a UK bank dealer.
"I wouldn't be surprised if the G7 were considering ways and means of stabilising currencies," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International in London.
But he said a scattergun approach to intervention at a few targeted currencies would probably be the first sign of protest.

The dollar climbed back above 1.79 marks after dipping to a session low of 1.7830 on Waigel's comments, and after popping over the 1.80 threshold was approaching Monday's U.S. high of 1.7995, its strongest since August 1991.
The pound traded close to Monday's 6-1/2-year high of 3.0239 marks, supported by expectations of a broad-based Economic and Monetary Union in Europe.
The dollar traded above 115 yen, boosted overnight from comments from Japanese Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara.
The official was reported to have said the G7 had no intention of using forex as a trade tool and that expectations of yen strength were too high.

The Dow industrials, which opened firmer, slipped to negative ground in early trade as the bond market also dipped. The bond market had at first strengthened after a 0.5 percent rise in June retail sales data, viewed as non-inflationary.
U.S. blue chips were seen needing the bond market's support to make gains, though technology stocks were sturdier amid optimism for second quarter earnings.
Germany's DAX index reached a new all-time record high at 4,154.98 points in post-bourse IBIS dealings, boosted by the dollar briefly trading above 1.80 marks and early gains on Wall Street.
Traders said the German market was growing nervous at current levels and saw the need for consolidation before further gains.
The UK's leading FTSE 100 index, which climbed to a record close on Monday, surged 0.8 percent to touch a new peak of 4,900 points on renewed interest in bank stocks.
"This market still wants to go higher," said the head of market-making at one leading brokerage. "There is a lot of liquidity looking for a solid safe home."
CURRENCIES AT 1330 GMT
The dollar was at 115.45 yen and 1.7980 marks compared with 113.88 yen and 1.7927 marks in late trading on Monday. STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was at 4,898.5, up 41.1 points.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 3.06 points at 4,121.13.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 2.58 at 2,944.17. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $319.75 compared to a previous close of $320.85.
Silver was at $4.26, down four cents from Monday's close.
